text: (Black-box rewinding access). For a probabilistic interactive oracle algorithm A and a fixed oracle function f , we write B f,A to denote that B has oracle access to f and black-box rewinding access to A relative to f : B can start executions of A, each with an independently sampled random tape, send messages to A to obtain its next message, rewind A to an earlier point of an execution (with the same random tape), and obtain the view of A in a completed execution (Definition 3.9). The oracle queries of A are answered by f , and they count toward the running time and query complexity of B.
